name: FMEA Decision Support Ontology
description: Detailed ontology for Failure Mode and Effects Analysis. It is designed to help an AI model reason from system context and function to failure modes, causes, effects, controls, risk ratings, actions, evidence, and residual risk across mechanical, electrical, electronic, software, control, thermal, fluidic, chemical, material, human, process, interface, environmental, cybersecurity, data/AI, maintenance, and supply-chain failure domains.

references.title: IEC 60812:2018
references.use: General FMEA/FMECA method anchor: planning, performing, documenting, maintaining, and identifying how items or processes fail to perform functions.

references.title: AIAG/VDA FMEA Handbook
references.use: Seven-step FMEA workflow: planning and preparation, structure analysis, function analysis, failure analysis, risk analysis, optimization, and results documentation.

references.title: SAE J1739
references.use: Design FMEA, Process FMEA, and supplemental FMEA-MSR reference.

references.title: ISO 14971 risk-management thinking
references.use: Hazard, foreseeable sequence of events, hazardous situation, harm, and risk-control logic for safety-related contexts.

reasoning_rules.statement: Before proposing failure modes, identify the intended function, operating mode, environment, input, output, performance parameter, and requirement.
Do not mix failure mode, cause, and effect. A failure mode is what goes wrong with the function; a cause is why it happens; an effect is what happens because of it.
Always ask for local effect, next-higher-level effect, system effect, end-user effect, and safety/regulatory/business effect when relevant.

For every important function, sweep across mechanical, electrical, electronic, software, control, thermal, fluidic, chemical, material, human, process, interface, environmental, cybersecurity, data/AI, maintenance, and supply-chain domains.
Treat interfaces as high-risk zones because mismatched assumptions, timing, units, tolerance, protocol, or responsibility boundaries often create hidden failures.
Ratings and claims about controls should cite evidence: test data, field data, simulations, inspections, process capability, supplier records, or expert rationale.
A current control must state what it controls: cause prevention, failure detection, effect mitigation, diagnostic monitoring, or response.
Every recommended action should explicitly target severity, occurrence, detection, diagnostic coverage, uncertainty, or traceability.
After actions, reassess severity, occurrence, detection/action priority, and record residual risk with acceptance rationale.
If key context is missing, ask targeted questions instead of inventing assumptions; if forced to proceed, mark assumptions explicitly.

nodes.label: FMEA Ontology
nodes.title: Semantic map for FMEA reasoning
nodes.description: Connects system structure, functions, failure modes, causes, effects, controls, risk scoring, and AI question prompts.

nodes.label: AI FMEA Facilitator
nodes.title: Guides an AI model to ask function-first failure analysis questions
nodes.description: Uses the ontology to check missing context, classify failure types, detect weak causal reasoning, and suggest follow-up questions.

nodes.label: FMEA Study
nodes.title: A bounded FMEA activity for a specific item, process, service, or system
nodes.description: Defines what is analyzed, why, by whom, under which assumptions, and with which scoring criteria.

nodes.label: FMEA Record
nodes.title: A single row or case in the FMEA table
nodes.description: Links one function to one failure mode, its effects, causes, controls, ratings, actions, and residual risk.

nodes.label: IEC 60812:2018
nodes.title: International FMEA and FMECA procedure reference
nodes.description: Useful as the general method anchor for planning, performing, documenting, maintaining FMEA/FMECA, and identifying how items or processes may fail to perform functions.

nodes.label: AIAG/VDA FMEA Handbook
nodes.title: Automotive seven-step FMEA structure
nodes.description: Useful for structuring FMEA as planning, structure analysis, function analysis, failure analysis, risk analysis, optimization, and results documentation.

nodes.label: SAE J1739
nodes.title: DFMEA, PFMEA, and supplemental FMEA-MSR reference
nodes.description: Useful for design, process, and monitoring/system-response FMEA in automotive and related engineering contexts.

nodes.label: ISO 14971 Risk Thinking
nodes.title: Hazard, hazardous situation, harm, and risk-control reasoning
nodes.description: Useful when FMEA must connect technical failure modes to foreseeable sequences of events, hazards, harms, and risk controls, especially in medical or safety-related systems.

nodes.label: Planning and Preparation
nodes.title: Define purpose, scope, team, assumptions, and analysis boundaries
nodes.description: Prevents the AI from analyzing the whole universe; FMEA without scope becomes engineering soup.

nodes.label: Structure Analysis
nodes.title: Break down the system, process, interfaces, and hierarchy
nodes.description: Answers: what parts exist and how are they connected?

nodes.label: Function Analysis
nodes.title: Identify intended functions, requirements, operating modes, and performance parameters
nodes.description: Failure modes should be derived from functions, not guessed randomly.

nodes.label: Failure Analysis
nodes.title: Identify failure modes, effects, causes, and mechanisms
nodes.description: Connects what can go wrong, why it goes wrong, and what happens next.

nodes.label: Risk Analysis
nodes.title: Score or rank severity, occurrence, detection, criticality, or action priority
nodes.description: Helps prioritize the scary monsters instead of treating every gremlin equally.

nodes.label: Optimization
nodes.title: Select and verify actions that reduce risk
nodes.description: Turns FMEA from a spreadsheet cemetery into actual engineering improvement.

nodes.label: Results Documentation
nodes.title: Capture decisions, evidence, residual risk, and lessons learned
nodes.description: Makes the analysis reusable, auditable, and traceable.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.title: Defines what is inside and outside the FMEA
nodes.description: Include product/process name, lifecycle phase, customer, use context, interfaces, exclusions, and depth of analysis.
ai_questions: What exactly are we analyzing?
What is explicitly out of scope?
Why is this boundary chosen?

nodes.label: System Boundary
nodes.title: Separates the analyzed item from external systems
nodes.description: Prevents blaming external systems without modeling the interface.
ai_questions: Where does responsibility transfer to another system or team?
Which inputs and outputs cross the boundary?

nodes.label: Item
nodes.title: The top-level object being analyzed
nodes.description: Can be a product, process step, subsystem, software service, medical device, robot, manufacturing operation, or organization process.

nodes.label: System
nodes.title: A set of interacting elements with a purpose
nodes.description: The top object when FMEA is performed at system level.

nodes.label: Subsystem
nodes.title: A major part of a system
nodes.description: Useful for hierarchical effects: local, next-level, system-level, user-level.

nodes.label: Component
nodes.title: A physical, software, human, or process element
nodes.description: Small enough to have concrete functions and failure modes.

nodes.label: Interface
nodes.title: Connection where energy, material, information, force, fluid, heat, or control crosses elements
nodes.description: Many failures hide at interfaces because each side says, 'not my circus, not my monkeys.'
ai_questions: What crosses this interface?
What assumptions does each side make?
What happens if the interface is late, noisy, leaky, blocked, reversed, overloaded, or incompatible?

nodes.label: Environment
nodes.title: External physical, cyber, operational, regulatory, and organizational conditions
nodes.description: Include temperature, humidity, vibration, EMC, contamination, users, network, workload, and maintenance setting.

nodes.label: Lifecycle Phase
nodes.title: Phase where the failure can occur or be detected
nodes.description: Examples: concept, design, manufacturing, transport, installation, operation, maintenance, update, decommissioning.

nodes.label: Operating Mode
nodes.title: Mode or state in which functions and failures differ
nodes.description: Examples: startup, normal operation, degraded mode, emergency stop, calibration, cleaning, charging, shutdown.

nodes.label: Use Scenario
nodes.title: A realistic sequence of user, system, and environment interactions
nodes.description: Useful for finding context-dependent failures.

nodes.label: Stakeholder
nodes.title: Person or organization affected by the function, failure, risk, or decision
nodes.description: Examples: user, patient, operator, maintainer, manufacturer, regulator, supplier, service team.

nodes.label: Requirement
nodes.title: A documented need, constraint, or performance expectation
nodes.description: Failure analysis should trace back to requirements when possible.
ai_questions: Which requirement is violated if this function fails?
Is the requirement measurable or ambiguous?

nodes.label: Assumption
nodes.title: A condition believed true but not yet proven
nodes.description: Assumptions should be visible because hidden assumptions are failure-mode factories.

nodes.label: Function
nodes.title: Intended action of an item under defined conditions
nodes.description: Write as verb + object + measurable target when possible, e.g., 'limit motor current below 5 A'.
ai_questions: What must this item do?
Why does this function matter?
What measurable parameter proves it works?

nodes.label: Primary Function
nodes.title: Main reason the item exists
nodes.description: Failure of a primary function often drives high severity.

nodes.label: Secondary Function
nodes.title: Supporting function needed for operation, usability, safety, or compliance
nodes.description: Often forgotten until it fails spectacularly, like a tiny screw with main-character energy.

nodes.label: Safety Function
nodes.title: Function that prevents or reduces harm
nodes.description: Examples: stop motion, isolate energy, limit temperature, alarm user, enter safe state.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Function
nodes.title: Function that detects, reports, or isolates faults
nodes.description: Important for detection rating and monitoring-response FMEA.

nodes.label: Performance Parameter
nodes.title: Measurable variable that defines function quality
nodes.description: Examples: torque, voltage, response time, accuracy, temperature, flow rate, pressure, current, latency.

nodes.label: Functional Chain
nodes.title: Ordered set of functions across components or process steps
nodes.description: Useful to ask: if upstream output fails, what downstream function fails next?

nodes.label: Input
nodes.title: Energy, material, information, command, or condition entering a function
nodes.description: Inputs can fail by being absent, wrong, noisy, late, early, too high, too low, or incompatible.

nodes.label: Output
nodes.title: Energy, material, information, command, product state, or service result produced by a function
nodes.description: Outputs become effects or causes for other elements.

nodes.label: Constraint
nodes.title: A limit on function, design, process, or operation
nodes.description: Examples: mass limit, cost limit, regulatory limit, voltage limit, sterilization condition.

nodes.label: Failure Mode
nodes.title: The specific way a function, item, or process can fail
nodes.description: Best phrased as a deviation from intended function: no, partial, degraded, intermittent, unintended, wrong, early, late, unstable, or out-of-tolerance.
ai_questions: How can this function fail?
Is this phrased as a problem, not a cause or effect?
What would an observer see?

nodes.label: Failure Effect
nodes.title: Consequence of a failure mode
nodes.description: Effects should be described at local, next-higher, system, user, safety, business, and regulatory levels where relevant.
ai_questions: What happens immediately?
Who notices?
What is the worst credible consequence?

nodes.label: Local Effect
nodes.title: Effect on the same component or process step
nodes.description: Useful for technical diagnosis.

nodes.label: Next Higher Level Effect
nodes.title: Effect on subsystem, process output, or downstream function
nodes.description: Connects local faults to system behavior.

nodes.label: End User Effect
nodes.title: Effect experienced by customer, user, patient, operator, or maintainer
nodes.description: Important for severity and communication.

nodes.label: Failure Cause
nodes.title: Reason the failure mode occurs
nodes.description: Should be controllable or testable when possible, not vague like 'bad design'.
ai_questions: Why would this failure mode happen?
Can this cause be prevented, detected, or verified?

nodes.label: Root Cause
nodes.title: Deeper cause that explains the origin of one or more direct causes
nodes.description: Useful for corrective action and lessons learned.

nodes.label: Failure Mechanism
nodes.title: Physical, logical, chemical, human, cyber, or process mechanism causing failure
nodes.description: Examples: fatigue crack growth, corrosion, memory leak, adhesive cure failure, calibration drift.

nodes.label: Hazard
nodes.title: Potential source of harm
nodes.description: Examples: electrical energy, sharp edge, stored pressure, toxic substance, moving actuator, wrong medical advice.

nodes.label: Hazardous Situation
nodes.title: Circumstance where people, assets, or environment are exposed to a hazard
nodes.description: Connects technical failures to real-world harm scenarios.

nodes.label: Harm
nodes.title: Injury, damage, loss, or adverse impact
nodes.description: Can include safety, mission, financial, legal, environmental, reputational, or user-trust harm.

nodes.label: Risk Concept
nodes.title: Combination of severity and likelihood, with detectability or controllability where the method uses it
nodes.description: Risk should not be a vibe. Vibes are for music, not safety decisions.

nodes.label: Severity
nodes.title: Seriousness of the effect if the failure occurs
nodes.description: Usually based on worst credible effect, not how easy the fix is.

nodes.label: Occurrence
nodes.title: Estimated likelihood or frequency of the cause or failure mode
nodes.description: Should use evidence such as field data, test data, process capability, supplier history, or expert judgment.

nodes.label: Detection Rating
nodes.title: Ability of current controls to detect cause or failure before the effect reaches the user
nodes.description: High detectability lowers risk priority only if detection is realistic and timely.

nodes.label: Risk Priority Number
nodes.title: Traditional score calculated from severity, occurrence, and detection
nodes.description: Useful but can hide priority differences; do not use blindly.

nodes.label: Action Priority
nodes.title: Priority classification for action based on severity, occurrence, and detection
nodes.description: Often preferred in AIAG/VDA-style FMEA over relying only on RPN.

nodes.label: Criticality
nodes.title: Severity-weighted likelihood or mission/safety importance of a failure mode
nodes.description: Common in FMECA or reliability-centered analyses.

nodes.label: Risk Acceptance Criteria
nodes.title: Defined threshold or rationale for acceptable residual risk
nodes.description: Must be explicit before arguing that a scary thing is 'probably fine'.

nodes.label: Current Control
nodes.title: Existing prevention, detection, verification, or monitoring activity
nodes.description: Controls must be specific and linked to causes or failure modes.

nodes.label: Prevention Control
nodes.title: Control that reduces occurrence by preventing the cause
nodes.description: Examples: design margin, derating, poka-yoke, supplier control, validated procedure.

nodes.label: Detection Control
nodes.title: Control that increases chance of detecting cause, failure mode, or effect
nodes.description: Examples: inspection, test, diagnostic, alarm, end-of-line validation.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Monitoring
nodes.title: Runtime detection, isolation, prediction, or response to faults
nodes.description: Important for monitored systems, connected products, robots, AI services, and safety-critical software.

nodes.label: Recommended Action
nodes.title: Risk-reduction action assigned after analysis
nodes.description: Should target severity, occurrence, or detection with clear owner and evidence.

nodes.label: Action Owner
nodes.title: Person or role responsible for completing the action
nodes.description: No owner means the action is an orphan. Orphans do not close risks.

nodes.label: Action Deadline
nodes.title: Due date or decision milestone for the action
nodes.description: Connects FMEA to project execution.

nodes.label: Verification Evidence
nodes.title: Proof that action or control works
nodes.description: Examples: test report, simulation result, inspection data, requirement trace, field data, audit record.

nodes.label: Residual Risk
nodes.title: Risk remaining after controls and actions
nodes.description: Must be accepted, reduced further, transferred, or escalated.

nodes.label: Lessons Learned
nodes.title: Reusable learning from failure, testing, field data, or previous FMEAs
nodes.description: Prevents the organization from stepping on the same rake with enthusiasm.

nodes.label: System FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes failures at system architecture and interaction level
nodes.description: Best for early design, interfaces, functions, emergent behavior, and system-level hazards.

nodes.label: Design FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes product or design failure modes before design release
nodes.description: Focuses on whether the design itself can meet functions and requirements.

nodes.label: Process FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes manufacturing, assembly, service, or business-process failure modes
nodes.description: Focuses on process steps, human actions, equipment, materials, methods, measurements, and environment.

nodes.label: FMEA-MSR
nodes.title: Supplemental FMEA for monitoring and system response
nodes.description: Focuses on runtime faults, diagnostic coverage, warning strategy, safe state, and controllability.

nodes.label: Software FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes software failure modes and their effects
nodes.description: Includes logic errors, timing, data, concurrency, interface, configuration, update, and exception handling failures.

nodes.label: Hardware FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes electronic, electrical, mechanical, and physical component failures
nodes.description: Often linked with reliability data, stress, derating, diagnostics, and environmental conditions.

nodes.label: FMECA
nodes.title: FMEA with criticality analysis
nodes.description: Adds criticality ranking or quantitative consequence/likelihood emphasis.

nodes.label: FMEDA
nodes.title: Failure Modes, Effects, and Diagnostic Analysis
nodes.description: Adds diagnostic coverage and failure-rate allocation, often used for safety integrity analysis.

nodes.label: Human Factors FMEA
nodes.title: Analyzes user, operator, maintainer, and organizational interaction failures
nodes.description: Useful for use error, poor instructions, cognitive load, alarms, training, and maintenance.

nodes.label: Mechanical Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving force, motion, geometry, structure, vibration, wear, tolerance, fatigue, or contact
nodes.description: Ask about loads, cycles, alignment, lubrication, vibration, clearance, stress concentration, and assembly fit.

nodes.label: Electrical Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving power, voltage, current, grounding, insulation, wiring, or energy distribution
nodes.description: Ask about shorts, opens, overload, transients, grounding, connector quality, insulation, and supply margins.

nodes.label: Electronic Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving electronic components, PCBs, sensors, actuators, ICs, solder, or EMC
nodes.description: Ask about drift, noise, component aging, ESD, EMI, thermal stress, firmware-hardware interaction, and diagnostic coverage.

nodes.label: Software Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving code, algorithms, configuration, state, timing, data, APIs, or updates
nodes.description: Ask about assumptions, exceptions, race conditions, invalid states, rollback, versioning, logging, and test coverage.

nodes.label: Control/System Dynamics Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving feedback loops, stability, estimation, actuation, or control logic
nodes.description: Ask about sensor delay, actuator saturation, model mismatch, unstable loop, calibration, and failover.

nodes.label: Thermal Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving heat generation, heat transfer, cooling, thermal runaway, or temperature limits
nodes.description: Ask about hotspots, cooling path, duty cycle, ambient temperature, insulation, and thermal derating.

nodes.label: Fluidic/Pneumatic/Hydraulic Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving liquid, gas, pressure, flow, valves, pumps, seals, or contamination
nodes.description: Ask about leakage, blockage, cavitation, pressure spikes, filter clogging, viscosity, and seal compatibility.

nodes.label: Chemical Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving reaction, degradation, corrosion, contamination, toxicity, flammability, or material compatibility
nodes.description: Ask about chemicals, exposure, cleaning agents, humidity, pH, oxidation, and storage conditions.

nodes.label: Material Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving material selection, defects, aging, microstructure, creep, fatigue, or environmental degradation
nodes.description: Ask about material grade, supplier variation, heat treatment, defects, fatigue curves, and aging.

nodes.label: Human Error / Use Error
nodes.title: Failure involving user, operator, maintainer, or team action/inaction
nodes.description: Ask whether the system invites the error, not whether humans are 'stupid'. Usually the interface is the sneaky raccoon.

nodes.label: Process Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving manufacturing, assembly, service, logistics, business workflow, or quality process
nodes.description: Ask about process step, method, machine, material, measurement, manpower, and environment.

nodes.label: Interface Failure
nodes.title: Failure at the boundary between components, teams, systems, users, or organizations
nodes.description: Ask about incompatible assumptions, timing, units, protocols, tolerances, physical fit, and responsibility handoff.

nodes.label: Environmental Failure
nodes.title: Failure caused or triggered by environment
nodes.description: Ask about temperature, humidity, dust, water, vibration, shock, altitude, salt fog, radiation, EMC, biofouling, and cleaning.

nodes.label: Cybersecurity Failure
nodes.title: Failure caused by malicious or unauthorized digital interaction
nodes.description: Ask about spoofing, tampering, denial of service, privilege misuse, insecure update, secrets, and data exfiltration.

nodes.label: Data / AI Failure
nodes.title: Failure involving data quality, model behavior, AI output, learning system drift, or decision support
nodes.description: Ask about bias, missing data, hallucination, confidence, monitoring, fallback, human override, and auditability.

nodes.label: Maintenance Failure
nodes.title: Failure caused by inadequate, incorrect, delayed, or impossible maintenance
nodes.description: Ask about maintainability, access, intervals, tooling, instructions, spare parts, and condition monitoring.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Failure
nodes.title: Failure caused by supplier, counterfeit, logistics, inventory, or specification mismatch
nodes.description: Ask about supplier qualification, change notification, traceability, substitute parts, and incoming inspection.

nodes.label: Loss of Function
nodes.title: Function is completely absent
nodes.description: Examples: motor does not start, software service unavailable, valve fails to open.

nodes.label: Partial Function
nodes.title: Function occurs but below required level
nodes.description: Examples: insufficient torque, weak signal, incomplete weld, low flow.

nodes.label: Degraded Function
nodes.title: Function quality worsens over time
nodes.description: Examples: sensor drift, wear, battery capacity loss, increasing latency.

nodes.label: Intermittent Function
nodes.title: Function appears and disappears unpredictably
nodes.description: Examples: loose connector, race condition, thermal intermittent fault.

nodes.label: Unintended Function
nodes.title: Item performs a function when it should not
nodes.description: Examples: actuator moves unexpectedly, alarm triggers falsely, software sends duplicate command.

nodes.label: Wrong Function
nodes.title: Wrong output, value, action, target, unit, state, or decision
nodes.description: Examples: wrong dose, wrong unit conversion, reversed polarity, wrong user record.

nodes.label: Early Function
nodes.title: Function occurs too early
nodes.description: Examples: premature release, early trigger, message sent before confirmation.

nodes.label: Late Function
nodes.title: Function occurs too late
nodes.description: Examples: delayed brake signal, slow alarm, late data synchronization.

nodes.label: Unstable / Oscillatory Function
nodes.title: Function oscillates, hunts, diverges, or becomes unstable
nodes.description: Examples: control loop instability, vibration chatter, repeated retry storm.

nodes.label: Out of Tolerance
nodes.title: Output or geometry outside allowed tolerance
nodes.description: Examples: dimension out of spec, voltage ripple high, temperature outside range.

nodes.label: Leakage
nodes.title: Unwanted escape of fluid, gas, energy, signal, current, or data
nodes.description: Examples: hydraulic leak, current leakage, memory leak, confidential data leak.

nodes.label: Blockage / Obstruction
nodes.title: Flow, movement, signal, or access is obstructed
nodes.description: Examples: clogged filter, blocked nozzle, jammed route, firewall blocking required traffic.

nodes.label: Fracture / Breakage
nodes.title: Crack, rupture, or break of a part
nodes.description: Ask about stress, defects, impact, fatigue, material, notch, and overload.

nodes.label: Fatigue
nodes.title: Progressive damage under cyclic loading
nodes.description: Ask about load cycles, vibration, stress concentration, surface finish, and fatigue limit.

nodes.label: Wear
nodes.title: Material loss or surface degradation due to contact and motion
nodes.description: Ask about lubrication, hardness, particles, alignment, contact pressure, and duty cycle.

nodes.label: Corrosion
nodes.title: Material degradation due to chemical or electrochemical reaction
nodes.description: Ask about humidity, salt, galvanic couples, coatings, cleaning agents, and exposure time.

nodes.label: Loosening
nodes.title: Fastener, connector, or fit loses intended retention
nodes.description: Ask about torque, vibration, locking method, thermal cycle, and assembly procedure.

nodes.label: Jamming / Sticking
nodes.title: Moving part cannot move or remains stuck
nodes.description: Ask about clearance, debris, lubrication, tolerance stack-up, deformation, and ice/dust.

nodes.label: Overheating
nodes.title: Temperature exceeds safe or functional limits
nodes.description: Ask about power dissipation, cooling, ambient, duty cycle, thermal path, and blocked ventilation.

nodes.label: Short Circuit
nodes.title: Unintended low-resistance electrical path
nodes.description: Ask about insulation, moisture, contamination, connector damage, solder bridge, and protection.

nodes.label: Open Circuit
nodes.title: Unintended interruption in electrical path
nodes.description: Ask about broken wire, connector disengagement, solder crack, fuse, switch, and vibration.

nodes.label: Insulation Breakdown
nodes.title: Loss of dielectric separation
nodes.description: Ask about voltage stress, aging, temperature, humidity, creepage, clearance, and contamination.

nodes.label: EMI/EMC Susceptibility
nodes.title: Performance affected by electromagnetic interference
nodes.description: Ask about shielding, grounding, cable routing, filtering, ESD, and immunity testing.

nodes.label: Sensor Drift
nodes.title: Sensor output gradually deviates from true value
nodes.description: Ask about calibration, temperature, aging, contamination, and self-diagnostics.

nodes.label: Actuator Stuck
nodes.title: Actuator remains stuck on, off, open, closed, or at a position
nodes.description: Ask about command signal, mechanical blockage, power loss, valve stiction, and fail-safe position.

nodes.label: Power Loss / Brownout
nodes.title: Power absent, unstable, or below required level
nodes.description: Ask about supply margin, battery, wiring, fuse, inrush, load transient, and backup power.

nodes.label: Communication Loss
nodes.title: Required data exchange unavailable, delayed, corrupted, or incompatible
nodes.description: Ask about protocol, timeout, retry, bandwidth, network, message schema, and fallback.

nodes.label: Software Crash
nodes.title: Process, service, task, or controller stops unexpectedly
nodes.description: Ask about exceptions, memory, watchdog, resource exhaustion, dependency failure, and recovery.

nodes.label: Timing / Race Condition
nodes.title: Behavior depends on unsafe timing or event ordering
nodes.description: Ask about concurrency, locks, interrupts, asynchronous messages, scheduling, and state transitions.

nodes.label: Data Corruption
nodes.title: Stored or transmitted data becomes wrong, incomplete, stale, duplicated, or inconsistent
nodes.description: Ask about validation, checksum, transaction, schema, time stamp, synchronization, and recovery.

nodes.label: AI Model Misclassification
nodes.title: AI model produces wrong class, recommendation, or interpretation
nodes.description: Ask about training data, distribution shift, confidence, edge cases, explainability, and human review.

nodes.label: Requirement Ambiguity
nodes.title: Requirement is unclear, incomplete, conflicting, unverifiable, or interpreted differently
nodes.description: Ask: which word can two engineers interpret differently? That word is probably the tiny chaos goblin.

nodes.label: Design Weakness
nodes.title: Design lacks margin, robustness, compatibility, diagnosability, or safe behavior
nodes.description: Ask whether the failure is designed-in rather than produced by manufacturing.

nodes.label: Manufacturing Defect
nodes.title: Part or product deviates from design intent during manufacturing
nodes.description: Examples: wrong dimension, poor solder, void, burr, incorrect cure, contamination.

nodes.label: Assembly Error
nodes.title: Incorrect assembly, orientation, torque, connection, routing, or configuration
nodes.description: Ask about poka-yoke, work instructions, fixtures, visual inspection, and training.

nodes.label: Contamination
nodes.title: Unwanted material affects function
nodes.description: Examples: dust, oil, water, particles, microbes, flux residue, metal shavings.

nodes.label: Overload
nodes.title: Load, stress, current, pressure, data traffic, or usage exceeds design capability
nodes.description: Ask about worst-case assumptions and abnormal but foreseeable use.

nodes.label: Aging / Degradation
nodes.title: Performance reduces over time due to aging, wear, chemical change, or fatigue
nodes.description: Ask about lifetime, cycles, storage, maintenance, and degradation monitoring.

nodes.label: Supplier Variation
nodes.title: Supplier part, material, process, or documentation varies from expectation
nodes.description: Ask about specification, qualification, substitutions, certificates, and change notification.

nodes.label: Use Error / Misuse
nodes.title: User action differs from intended use, including foreseeable misuse
nodes.description: Ask whether design, labeling, training, or workflow makes the misuse likely.

nodes.label: Inadequate Maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance is omitted, late, wrong, undocumented, or impossible under real conditions
nodes.description: Ask about access, tools, intervals, instructions, and condition-based monitoring.

nodes.label: External Event
nodes.title: External shock, outage, disaster, regulatory change, cyber event, or environmental condition triggers failure
nodes.description: Ask what external events are credible, not just convenient.

nodes.label: Cyberattack
nodes.title: Malicious digital action causes unsafe, unavailable, incorrect, or unauthorized behavior
nodes.description: Ask about threat actor, attack surface, authentication, logging, and isolation.

nodes.label: Software Defect
nodes.title: Bug, configuration error, logic error, dependency problem, or update fault causes failure
nodes.description: Ask about tests, versioning, rollback, observability, and exception handling.

nodes.label: Design Review
nodes.title: Structured review of design intent, interfaces, assumptions, margins, and failure logic
nodes.description: Good for catching conceptual and interface failures early.

nodes.label: Simulation / Analysis
nodes.title: Model-based analysis of behavior under nominal, worst-case, and fault conditions
nodes.description: Examples: dynamics simulation, circuit simulation, thermal model, process simulation.

nodes.label: Tolerance Stack-up Analysis
nodes.title: Checks whether geometric and process variation can break function
nodes.description: Useful for fit, alignment, leakage, jamming, and out-of-tolerance failures.

nodes.label: Finite Element Analysis
nodes.title: Analyzes stress, strain, vibration, thermal behavior, or structural margins
nodes.description: Useful for fracture, fatigue, deformation, and thermal-mechanical problems.

nodes.label: Fault Tree Analysis
nodes.title: Top-down logic analysis from undesired event to combinations of causes
nodes.description: Complements FMEA by asking how causes combine.

nodes.label: Test and Validation
nodes.title: Empirical proof under defined conditions that item or process meets needs
nodes.description: Must be tied to requirements, failure modes, and acceptance criteria.

nodes.label: Inspection
nodes.title: Examination, measurement, or audit to detect defects or nonconformance
nodes.description: Can be visual, dimensional, electrical, software, document, or process inspection.

nodes.label: Poka-Yoke / Error Proofing
nodes.title: Design or process feature that prevents incorrect action or assembly
nodes.description: Best when humans are involved and mistakes are predictable.

nodes.label: Redundancy
nodes.title: Additional element or path that maintains function after a failure
nodes.description: Can reduce severity or occurrence of system effect but may add complexity.

nodes.label: Derating
nodes.title: Operating component below maximum rating to improve reliability
nodes.description: Common for electrical, thermal, mechanical, and material stress.

nodes.label: Safety Margin
nodes.title: Difference between expected load/stress and capability/limit
nodes.description: Useful but should be justified by evidence, not optimism wearing a lab coat.

nodes.label: Fail-Safe State
nodes.title: Defined state that minimizes harm when failure is detected or likely
nodes.description: Examples: stop motion, open valve, close valve, isolate power, disable output.

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation
nodes.title: Reduced but controlled functionality after partial failure
nodes.description: Useful for resilience and user trust.

nodes.label: Alarm / Alert
nodes.title: Signal that informs user, operator, maintainer, or system about abnormal condition
nodes.description: Must be timely, understandable, actionable, and not alarm-spam confetti.

nodes.label: Maintenance Plan
nodes.title: Scheduled or condition-based tasks to preserve function
nodes.description: Includes inspection, replacement, calibration, cleaning, lubrication, and software updates.

nodes.label: Training / Instruction
nodes.title: Human guidance for correct operation, assembly, service, or response
nodes.description: Should not be the only control for high-severity risks if design control is possible.

nodes.label: Change Control
nodes.title: Process for evaluating and approving changes to design, process, software, supplier, or requirement
nodes.description: Prevents 'small harmless change' from becoming a dragon with a clipboard.

nodes.label: Traceability
nodes.title: Links requirements, functions, design elements, tests, risks, actions, and evidence
nodes.description: Helps AI explain why a failure matters and what evidence closes it.

nodes.label: Context Questions
nodes.title: Questions that define scope, environment, lifecycle, assumptions, and stakeholders
nodes.description: Use before generating failure modes.

nodes.label: Function Questions
nodes.title: Questions that elicit intended function, measurable outputs, and operating modes
nodes.description: Use to derive failure modes from what the item must do.

nodes.label: Interface Questions
nodes.title: Questions about exchanged energy, material, information, force, heat, fluid, or control
nodes.description: Use to find failures hidden between parts, teams, or systems.

nodes.label: Failure Mode Questions
nodes.title: Questions that transform each function into possible deviations
nodes.description: Use patterns: no, partial, degraded, intermittent, unintended, wrong, early, late, unstable, out-of-tolerance.

nodes.label: Effect Questions
nodes.title: Questions that trace consequences from local effect to end-user or harm
nodes.description: Use to avoid confusing effects with causes.

nodes.label: Cause Questions
nodes.title: Questions that find physical, logical, process, human, environmental, and cyber causes
nodes.description: Use repeated 'why' carefully until a controllable or testable cause appears.

nodes.label: Control Questions
nodes.title: Questions that identify prevention, detection, diagnostic, monitoring, and response controls
nodes.description: Use to check whether current controls actually target the cause or failure mode.

nodes.label: Evidence Questions
nodes.title: Questions about data, tests, simulation, inspections, field history, and confidence
nodes.description: Use to separate engineering knowledge from confident guessing.

nodes.label: Counterfactual Questions
nodes.title: Questions that ask what must be true for the failure not to occur
nodes.description: Useful for finding missing controls and assumptions.

nodes.label: Cross-Domain Questions
nodes.title: Questions that force review across mechanical, electrical, software, human, process, cyber, and environmental domains
nodes.description: Useful because failures love wearing disguises.

nodes.label: Missing Information Questions
nodes.title: Questions that identify unknowns blocking reliable analysis
nodes.description: Use to ask for drawings, requirements, schematics, process maps, data, supplier specs, and operating context.

nodes.label: Prioritization Questions
nodes.title: Questions that rank risks and actions
nodes.description: Use to decide what to address first based on severity, occurrence, detection, criticality, uncertainty, and stakeholder impact.

edges.label: can deviate as
edges.question_prompt: For this function, what does no/partial/degraded/intermittent/unintended/wrong/early/late/unstable/out-of-tolerance look like?

edges.label: clarifies
edges.question_prompt: What exactly is the item, boundary, lifecycle phase, use scenario, and environment?

edges.label: elicits
edges.question_prompt: What must the item do, for whom, under which mode, and how is success measured?

edges.label: probes
edges.question_prompt: What crosses the interface, in which direction, under which timing, tolerance, protocol, or compatibility assumption?

edges.label: generates
edges.question_prompt: For each function, how can it be absent, partial, degraded, intermittent, unintended, wrong, early, late, unstable, or out-of-tolerance?

edges.label: traces
edges.question_prompt: What happens locally, downstream, at system level, to the user, and in the worst credible case?

edges.label: elicits
edges.question_prompt: Why would this failure mode occur mechanically, electrically, electronically, in software, by process, by user interaction, by environment, by supplier, or by cyber event?

edges.label: checks
edges.question_prompt: What currently prevents the cause, detects the failure, alerts the user, isolates the fault, or moves the system to a safe state?

edges.label: requests
edges.question_prompt: What data, test, simulation, inspection, field history, or expert source supports the rating and control claim?

edges.label: suggests
edges.question_prompt: What design, process, interface, monitoring, or training change would make this failure impossible or less likely?

edges.label: broadens
edges.question_prompt: Could this same effect be caused by mechanical, electrical, software, human, process, environmental, cyber, or data/AI failure?

edges.label: surfaces
edges.question_prompt: What are we assuming because drawings, requirements, schematics, logs, test data, supplier specs, or process maps are missing?

edges.label: prioritizes
edges.question_prompt: Which action is justified first given severity, occurrence, detection, uncertainty, stakeholder harm, and feasibility?
